statements.impact_statement: katex 0.16.47 is pulled in only by mermaid 11, which pins ^0.16.45; the fix is in 0.18.2. mermaid 12.2.0 moves to katex 0.18, but it needs @mermaid-js/layout-elk 1.x, and layout-elk 1.0.1 (latest) still depends on katex ^0.16.47 and inlines 0.16.47 in its ESM bundle. The only place katex code runs is the CLI --export-diagrams renderer, which serves the self-contained mermaid and layout-elk ESM bundles with their own inlined katex copies, so an npm override cannot reach the code that executes. katex loads only when a diagram contains a math block. The advisory describes a read-side prototype pollution gadget: it needs an already-polluted Object.prototype plus attacker-controlled math input, and no CALM component pollutes the prototype or renders untrusted math.

statements.impact_statement: ip-address 10.7.2 is bundled inside npm 11.21.1, which is pulled in only by @semantic-release/npm for the CLI release job. It is not part of the published @finos/calm-cli package. npm overrides cannot change a bundled dependency, and no npm release bundles the fix (10.7.4) yet: npm 12.2.1 also bundles 10.7.2. Inside npm, socks passes Address6 only the registry and proxy hosts from npm config, which the release workflow sets, so an attacker cannot supply the long zone identifier that causes the slow parse. The other ip-address copy in the lockfile is 10.7.4.

statements.impact_statement: @sveltejs/kit 2.70.2 is used only by the CALM Studio app, a single-page app built with adapter-static for the web and the desktop app (ssr = false, prerender = false, index.html fallback). The flaw is in prerendered pages that set a cache-control header from an untrusted source with setHeaders. CALM Studio prerenders no pages, has no server routes and does not call setHeaders. The fix is only in kit 3, which needs TypeScript 6.

statements.impact_statement: @sveltejs/kit 2.70.2 is used only by the CALM Studio app, a single-page app built with adapter-static. The flaw is an open redirect in enhanced form actions (use:enhance) on routes that accept paths that begin with //. CALM Studio has only the root route, no form actions and no use:enhance. The fix is only in kit 3, which needs TypeScript 6.

statements.impact_statement: deepmerge 4.3.1 is a build-time dependency only. @sveltejs/vite-plugin-svelte uses it in the CALM Studio app and @calmstudio/diagram builds to merge the project-owned Svelte and Vite config. @svgr/plugin-svgo, through Docusaurus preset-classic in the docs site, declares it but never imports it. statements.impact_statement: opentelemetry-api 1.62.0 comes in through the Quarkus 3.40 BOM. The flaw is quadratic CPU use when the W3C propagator parses an inbound tracestate header. CALM Hub turns off the OpenTelemetry SDK by default (CALM_OTEL_DISABLED=true). Quarkus then builds a no-op SDK and disables the HTTP server instrumenter, so it does not parse tracestate. A deployment that sets CALM_OTEL_DISABLED=false is exposed. The fix (1.67.0) cannot be overridden, because Quarkus 3.40 does not start with OpenTelemetry 1.67. Quarkus 3.40.1.1, the latest 3.40 LTS release, still manages 1.62.0, and only the Quarkus 4.0 pre-releases move on. It needs a Quarkus release that manages OpenTelemetry 1.67.0 or later.

statements.impact_statement: glob 13.0.6 is bundled inside npm 11.21.1, which is pulled in only by @semantic-release/npm for the CLI release job. It is not part of the published @finos/calm-cli package. npm overrides cannot change a bundled dependency, and no npm release bundles the fix (14.0.2): npm 12.2.1 also bundles 13.0.6. The flaw is that a walk keeps reading directories after its AbortSignal fires. npm never passes a signal to glob, so no walk is aborted. The other glob copy in the lockfile is 14.0.3, which has the fix.

statements.impact_statement: The flaw is unbounded growth of globParts in the preprocessing that minimatch runs at optimizationLevel 2 or higher. minimatch 3.1.5 comes in through @stoplight/spectral-core (in @finos/calm-shared, so the CLI, the VS Code extension and CALM Lab), serve-handler (Docusaurus), and eslint and its plugins (development only). minimatch 3 has no optimizationLevel option and no such preprocessing, so the vulnerable code is not present. An override to 11.x is not possible, because minimatch 11 has a different export shape. minimatch 10.2.5 is bundled inside npm 11.21.1, which is pulled in only by @semantic-release/npm for the CLI release job and is not part of the published package. npm never sets optimizationLevel, so the default of 1 applies and the vulnerable code does not run. The other minimatch 10 copies are overridden to 11.0.4, which has the fix.
